arxiv-2203-09679.title: Modeling Intensification for Sign Language Generation: A Computational Approach
arxiv-2203-09679.creator: Mert İnan, Yang Zhong, Sabit Hassan, Lorna Quandt, Malihe Alikhani
arxiv-2203-09679.description: Abstract End-to-end sign language generation models do not accurately represent the prosody in sign language. A lack of temporal and spatial variations leads to poor-quality generated presentations that confuse human interpreters. In this paper, we aim to improve the prosody in generated sign languages by modeling intensification in a data-driven manner.

arxiv-2301-10281.title: Lightweight Neural Architecture Search for Temporal Convolutional Networks at the Edge
arxiv-2301-10281.creator: Matteo Risso, Alessio Burrello, Francesco Conti, Lorenzo Lamberti, Yukai Chen, Luca Benini, Enrico Macii, Massimo Poncino, and Daniele Jahier Pagliari
arxiv-2301-10281.description: Abstract Neural Architecture Search (NAS) is quickly becoming the go-to approach to optimize the structure of Deep Learning (DL) models for complex tasks such as Image Classification or Object Detection. However, many other relevant applications of DL, especially at the edge, are based on time-series processing and require models with unique features, for which NAS is less explored.

arxiv-2404-00840.title: A proposal for enhancing technosignature search toward the Galactic center
arxiv-2404-00840.creator: Naoki Seto
arxiv-2404-00840.description: Abstract We discuss the possibility of enhancing intelligent life searches toward the Galactic center. From the clockwork orbital motions of stars around the Sgr A ∗ black hole, we can determine the distance to the Galactic center at an exceptional accuracy, despite its remoteness ∼ 8.3 \sim 8.3 kpc.

arxiv-2405-04603.title: Neural network based approach for solving problems in plane wave duct acoustics
arxiv-2405-04603.creator: D. Veerababu, Prasanta K. Ghosh
arxiv-2405-04603.description: Abstract Neural networks have emerged as a tool for solving differential equations in many branches of engineering and science. But their progress in frequency domain acoustics is limited by the vanishing gradient problem that occurs at higher frequencies. This paper discusses a formulation that can address this issue.

arxiv-2407-09642.title: Seq-to-Final: A Benchmark for Tuning from Sequential Distributions to a Final Time Point
arxiv-2407-09642.creator: Christina X Ji, Ahmed M Alaa, David Sontag
arxiv-2407-09642.description: Abstract Distribution shift over time occurs in many settings. Leveraging historical data is necessary to learn a model for the last time point when limited data is available in the final period, yet few methods have been developed specifically for this purpose.

arxiv-2412-12468.description: Abstract . User targeting, the process of selecting targeted users from a pool of candidates for non-expert marketers, has garnered substantial attention with the advancements in digital marketing. However, existing user targeting methods encounter two significant challenges: (i) Poor cross-domain and cross-scenario transferability and generalization , and (ii) Insufficient forecastability in real-world applications .

arxiv-2507-01953.title: FreeMorph: Tuning-Free Generalized Image Morphing with Diffusion Model
arxiv-2507-01953.creator: Yukang Cao, Chenyang Si, Jinghao Wang, Ziwei Liu
arxiv-2507-01953.description: Abstract We present FreeMorph , the first tuning-free method for image morphing that accommodates inputs with different semantics or layouts. Unlike existing methods that rely on fine-tuning pre-trained diffusion models and are limited by time constraints and semantic/layout discrepancies, FreeMorph delivers high-fidelity image morphing without requiring per-instance training.

pmc-11391082.title: Analysis of oil accumulation mechanisms in plasma induced mutant Scenedesmus strains compared to original Scenedesmus strains
pmc-11391082.creator: Wenqian Wei, Feng Huang
pmc-11391082.description: Scenedesmus sp. is a species of the Scenedesmus genus within the phylum Chlorophyta, commonly found as a planktonic algal species in freshwater and known for its rapid growth rate. pmc-11727348.title: Assessment of the Peripheral and Central Auditory System in Infants Whose Mothers Tested Positive for COVID-19 During Pregnancy
pmc-11727348.creator: Jheniffer Queiroz Raimundo, Milaine Dominici Sanfins, Piotr Henryk Skarzynski, Magdalena Beata Skarżyńska, Maria Francisca Colella-Santos
pmc-11727348.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Introduction: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) is an infectious disease caused by the Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), a new member of the coronavirus family. While respiratory transmission is the main route, concerns have arisen regarding possible vertical transmission, which refers to the transmission of the virus from mother to fetus through the dissemination of viral particles in the amniotic fluid. Fetal viral infection via the placenta can affect the formation of the auditory system and lead to congenital hearing disorders.

pmc-12436890.title: Neuropsychiatric Disorders and Psychosis Induced by Chronic Toluene Exposure: Case Review and Antipsychotic Treatment Approaches
pmc-12436890.creator: A. Romero Teruel, A. Vives Luengo, P. Vazquez Giraldo, B. Franco Lovaco, G. Vega
pmc-12436890.description: IntroductionThis case of a 79-year-old patient with inferred past exposure to toluene and persistent paranoid delusions illustrates the potential neuropsychiatric consequences of solvent exposure. The patient’s work as a car painter (1990-1992) aligns with literature highlighting the neurotoxic effects of organic solvents.

pmc-12448767.title: Chronic rhinosinusitis: an underrecognized occupational disease
pmc-12448767.creator: Quentin Durand-Moreau
pmc-12448767.description: ronic rhinosinusitis is a typical occupational disease. Work-related rhinitis is usually classified under either occupational rhinitis, which is caused by work and can be either allergic or nonallergic (i.e., caused by workplace irritants); or work-exacerbated rhinitis, when a preexisting rhinitis is made worse by work.2 The exact prevalence of work-related rhinitis is unclear.

pmc-12470470.title: Electrocautery vs. Cold Cutting in Modified Radical Mastectomy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmc-12470470.creator: Dennis Cicio, Alin Gheorghe Balta, Teodora Livia Homorozan, Vladimir Ciornei, Octav Marius Russu, Horea Rares Benea, Mihai Pavel, Lorenzo Scardina
pmc-12470470.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background and Objectives: Modified radical mastectomy (MRM) is a common surgical procedure, with outcomes that are influenced by the instruments used in the operation. This meta-analysis aimed to compare “cold cutting” or “traditional” techniques and monopolar or bipolar electrocautery. Materials and Methods: A comprehensive search of five databases was conducted, with only studies of adult patients undergoing MRM in clearly defined groups selected. Data from 12 RCTs and 3 cohort studies summarizing 1372 participants was extracted and then synthesized using random-effects models.

pmc-12598332.title: Preoperative prediction of tumor budding in colorectal cancer based on quantitative parameters of dual-layer detector spectral computed tomography: a preliminary study
pmc-12598332.creator: Pengqiang Li, Nianjun Liu, Yanfei Wang, Jinhui Lan, Huling Ren, Jing Wang, Yu Dou
pmc-12598332.description: BackgroundTumor budding (TB) is an autonomous risk factor indicative of the invasiveness and prognosis of colorectal cancer (CRC). Dual-layer spectral detector computed tomography (SDCT) is a novel energy-resolved imaging technology that enables multiparametric tissue characterization through quantitative spectral analysis. Nevertheless, the efficacy of quantitative measures derived from SDCT in differentiating the TB grade of CRC remains ambiguous.

pmc-12694922.title: Zirconia abutments: Biological, mechanical, and esthetic considerations – An umbrella review of available systematic reviews and meta-analyses
pmc-12694922.creator: Amin Davoudi, Mahsa Abbasi, Negin Aminianpour, Kimia Salimian, Peyman Movahedian Attar
pmc-12694922.description: Zirconia abutments can enhance esthetics by providing a natural appearance due to their semitranslucency. Evidence for final outcomes of using zirconia abutments compared to other available materials are diverse. This study aims to review all available evidence from previous reviews to compare zirconia and titanium abutments regarding biological, mechanical, and esthetics indices and survival.

pmc-13353176.title: Exact Discrete Stochastic Simulation With Deep‐Learning‐Scale Gradient Optimization
pmc-13353176.creator: Jose M G Vilar, Leonor Saiz
pmc-13353176.description: Exact stochastic simulation of continuous‐time Markov chains (CTMCs) is essential when discreteness and noise drive system behavior, but the hard categorical event selection in Gillespie‐type algorithms blocks gradient‐based learning. We eliminate this constraint by decoupling forward simulation from backward differentiation, with hard categorical sampling generating exact trajectories and gradients propagating through a continuous massively‐parallel Gumbel‐Softmax straight‐through surrogate.

uslaw-usc-t21-s1403.title: 21 U.S.C. § 1403 — Pesticide analytical methods
uslaw-usc-t21-s1403.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t21-s1403.description: United States Code, Title 21 (Food And Drugs); Chapter 19 (Pesticide Monitoring Improvements). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The Secretary of Health and Human Services shall, in consultation with the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency— (1) develop a detailed long-range plan and timetable for research that is necessary for the development of and validation of— (A) new and improved analytical methods.
